Figure 1 • Physics Benchmark

Pristine Quantum Conductance Spectra Across All 13 Materials ($N=9$)

Caroli NEGF • Universal eV Grid ($0\dots 8.32$ eV)

Clean transmission spectra $T(E)$ calculated via Caroli non-equilibrium Green's function formalism contacted by semi-infinite pristine leads (Sancho-Rubio decimation). Each curve is an exact integer step counter of open propagating transverse subbands in the ribbon Brillouin zone.

Dirac Semimetals (Graphene, Silicene, Germanene)

Exhibit characteristic linear Dirac dispersion with quantized transmission steps $T = 0, 1, 2, 3\dots$ Conductance scales directly with the hopping amplitude: graphene ($t = 2.70$ eV) spans the full 8 eV window, while silicene ($t = 1.07$ eV) and germanene ($t = 0.99$ eV) compress the relativistic subband staircase into lower energies.

Semiconductors & TMDs (hBN, Phosphorene, MoS2, WS2, MoSe2, WSe2)

Exhibit prominent bandgaps where $T(E) = 0$: hBN has a wide $2.5$ eV insulator gap. Phosphorene shows sharp anisotropic subbands. The four TMD cousins feature dense multi-orbital $d$-bands reaching conductances of $12\dots 16\,G_0$. WSe2 N14 contains a subtle 0.9 meV mini-gap requiring specialized lead broadening.

Flat-Band & Metallic Lattices (Kagome, Lieb, Checkerboard, Triangular)

Showcase destructive quantum interference: Kagome displays prominent transmission peaks at the flat-band energy $E = +2.0t$. Lieb exhibits a zero-energy flat-band spike at $E = 0$. Checkerboard (planar pyrochlore) shows a localized flat-band plateau. Triangular metal features a wide, gapless metallic continuum.

Figure 2 • Disorder Physics

Fingerprint Evolution Under Anderson Disorder ($d = 0\%\dots 4\%$)

1,000 Seeds per Density • Median ± 10th-90th Percentile Spread

How microscopic atomic disorder transforms sharp quantum steps into identifiable continuous fingerprints. Showing Graphene (Dirac), MoS2 (multi-orbital TMD), hBN (insulator), and Kagome (flat band) across 4 disorder concentrations: $d \in [0.5\%, 1.0\%, 2.0\%, 4.0\%]$.

Key Physical Insights from Disorder Evolution:
  • Van Hove Singularity Smoothing: As disorder increases, elastic backscattering rounds off sharp subband thresholds without shifting overall band edge locations.
  • Strict Bulk Boundedness (Store Invariant): Disordered median conductance is strictly bounded from above by clean pristine limits (MaxExcess ≤ +0.0000), preserving the physical requirement that random defects cannot systematically enhance transmission.
  • Fingerprint Uniqueness: At moderate disorder ($1\%\dots 2\%$), the smoothed transmission profile retains high-frequency curvature markers unique to the device width and material, which the ensemble lookup exploits for 99.992% accuracy.
Figure 3 • Finite Size Confinement

Subband Staircase vs. Atomic Ribbon Width ($N$)

Demonstrating the quantum size effect across Graphene ($N=5\dots 20$), MoS2 ($N=7, 9, 14$), and Kagome ($N=7, 9, 14$). Wider ribbons pack more transverse modes, narrowing subband spacing and increasing conductance.

Notice the discrete $3p, 3p+1, 3p+2$ family oscillations in armchair graphene, which caused early continuous manifold models to fail and led to the adoption of modal majority voting.

Scientific Integrity

Forensic Bug Postmortems (Bugs #6–#11)

A critical summary of historical methodological and numerical traps identified, mathematically characterized, and eliminated.

Bug #6: Seed Leakage in Train/Val/Test Splits Fixed • Config-Seed Rule

Random row-wise slicing leaked the exact spatial defect configuration across concentration clouds because row $i$ of concentration $c_1$ and row $i$ of concentration $c_2$ shared the same pseudorandom seed. This falsely inflated neural accuracy to 99.9% while collapsing out-of-sample generalization.

Rule: Split strictly by configuration seed: row i belongs to test set iff seed i ≥ 850.
Bug #7: Label Leakage in Input Transforms Fixed • InputSpec v4

Early pipelines normalized energy by $E / t$ where $t$ is the material hopping parameter, or clipped transmission by ribbon width $N$. This required knowing the material identity before running the model.

Rule: All transforms must be label-free. Standardized to universal 416-channel eV grid [0, 8.32 eV].
Bug #8: Floating-Point Gap Leakage (The Round-First Rule) Fixed • Round-First (3 Decimals)

Dividing numerical transmission inside insulating bandgaps ($T pprox 10^{-7}$) by pristine values ($T pprox 10^{-6}$) caused 78% of bandgap channels to evaluate to ~1.0, generating fictitious conductivity in semiconductors.

Rule: Round T to 3 decimal places before any division or logarithmic transform.
Bug #9: Corrupted Square Lattice Benchmarks Fixed • ca_sq.py Engine

Square-lattice CSV benchmarks exported from early Jupyter notebooks had overwritten columns and phase shifts. Re-implemented via ca_sq.py with Sancho-Rubio decimation, achieving exact $10^{-8}$ agreement with analytic channel counts.

Bug #10: Multi-Orbital TMD Disorder Decoupling Fixed • Physical Atomic Defect Generator

Randomly shifting diagonal elements of the TMD Hamiltonian treated individual orbitals on the same atom independently, violating physical atomic defect physics.

Rule: Disorder generator picks physical Mo/W atom indices and shifts all 3 d-orbitals together with V = 0.2535 eV.
Bug #11: TMD N=14 Lead Decimation Mini-Gap Breakdown Fixed • Adaptive --lead-eta

In WSe2 N=14 ribbons, an ultra-narrow 0.9 meV mini-gap caused Sancho-Rubio decimation with default broadening $\eta = 10^{-6}$ to oscillate near convergence thresholds. Added configurable runtime `--lead-eta = 1e-5`, restoring 100% convergence.
